div.head: IV Eg 6
div.ab: ⁊ ælc mon mid heora gewitnysse bigcge ⁊ sylle ælc þara ceapa, þe he bigcge oððe sylle aþer oððe burge oððe on wæpengetace.
⁊ ælc mon mid heora gewytnyssa bigcge ⁊ sylle ælc þeora ceapa, þe he bicgcge oððe sylle aþer oððe burge oððe wæpengetace.
Si quis uero ciuis aut peregrinus, poscente usu necessitatis humane, quid emere uoluerit aut uendere, secum (uel sibi) sumat testimonium in omni negotio, sit in ciuitate, rure aut hundrode.
⁊ ælc mon mid heora gewytnysse bigcge ⁊ sylle ælc þeora ceapa þe he bicgcge oððe sylle aþer oððe burge oððe wæpengetace.
Und jedermann kaufe und verkaufe unter ihrer Zeugenschaft jedes der Kaufgeschäfte, das er kauft oder verkauft, entweder in Stadt oder in Wapentake.
And let every man buy and sell, with their witness, every one of the goods that he buys or sells, either in a borough or in a wapentake.
And every man shall buy or sell in the presence of these witnesses all the goods which he buys or sells either in a borough or in a wapentake.
And every man is with their witness to buy and sell all goods that he buys and sells, in either a borough or a wapentake.

u. s. written above by the scribe C
Noch nicht begegnet hier der Gewährbürge; s. d. Gl; Handel 8a
The warrantor does not yet appear here; see that word in Gl; Handel 8a
Wie burge so kann wæpengetace lokativer Instrumental sein, also das von F davor gesetzte on ursprünglich fehlen
Like burge, wæpengetace can be a locative instrumental, so that the on placed before it by F may originally have been absent

Vgl. o. 3².—Da Versio das Wapentake unterdrückt, rührt sie nicht aus Denalagu her; s. u. 12¹. Zu jenem steht hundred synonym o. 3, 1; u. 10. Nicht bloss die Gerichtsversammlung, sondern das Bezirksterritorium muss gemeint sein, da Viehhandel nicht bloss alle vier Wochen vorkam, da zweitens, wenn das Volk doch bei jedem Handel versammelt wäre, es nicht erst eines Kaufzeugen-Ausschusses bedurft hätte, und drittens dann der Hundred-Vorsteher jeden Handel gekannt hätte, nicht erst, wie hier 10, von den Kaufzeugen darüber unterrichtet zu werden brauchte

Cf. above 3².—Since the Versio suppresses the wapentake, it does not originate from the Denalagu; see below 12¹. Hundred is used as synonymous with it above 3, 1; below 10. Not merely the court assembly but the territory of the district must be meant, since cattle-dealing did not take place only every four weeks; since, secondly, if the people were in any case assembled at every transaction, there would have been no need for a committee of purchase-witnesses; and since, thirdly, the head of the hundred would then have known of every transaction, and would not first have needed, as here in 10, to be informed of it by the purchase-witnesses

The territorial division found in certain counties (the N. and W. Ridings of Yorkshire, Lincolnshire, Leicestershire, Nottinghamshire, Derbyshire and Rutland) corresponding more or less to the hundreds which are found in the southern counties. The term is generally explained from Ed. Conf. 30.
